messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: gpu-pool-eu-west-1 saturated, autoscaler erroring with scale_limit_reached, queue length growing > 18k, user-facing 503s starting ~00:03 UTC. Pager -> cal oncall.
cal: I'm on it. grabbing quick metrics. can someone throttle non-critical workloads (batch/embeddings) in eu-west-1? will start triage.
ryan: pulling autoscaler logs now, give me the pod name.
cal: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=autoscaler-eu` -> autoscaler-eu-6b7c8
cal: logs show repeated `scale_up failed: quotaExceeded` and `scale_down suppressed` noise. suspect provider quota + plan cap.
ryan: yikes. provider returned 429 / capacityLimitReached to scale API. autoscaler retries but hits internal limit flag. stack traces attached in logs.
maya: pinging cloud infra to confirm quota/offer. also can we failover traffic to backup-pool in eu-central? we have warm nodes there.
ops-bot: @maya incident created: INC-2026-1345, linked runbook: <link to runbook/queue-throttle>
cal: temp mitigation plan: 1) enable shedding for low-priority tenants 2) route new requests for heavy models to eu-central fallback model variant 3) increase autoscaler cap if provider allows 4) pause scheduled batch jobs.
june: on it — pausing batch job queue (job-agent command below)
june: ```
jobctl pause --cluster eu-west-1 --tag "batch" --reason "incident midnight spike"
```
liam: adding a temporary ingress rule to route /v1/generate for model-xl to eu-central with header override.
liam: ```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  route-override: |
    - match: /v1/generate
      rewrite: route:eu-central
EOF
EOF
```
cal: good. maya, any reply from cloud infra?
maya: cloud ops: "we hit regional soft quota for g4dn-like instances, can request temporary increase but 30-45m ETA." They also noted a pending outage on our reserved capacity sync.
ryan: we can't wait 30m. suggestion: enable model-fallback and dust-down quantized variant in-place to reduce GPU mem and allow twice the active sessions on same pool.
cal: can we toggle fallback at the gateway level? need quick toggle.
liam: yes — feature-flag `model_fallback_eu_west` exists. I can flip it now.
liam: flipped `model_fallback_eu_west=true` :thumbsup:
cal: traffic is shifting, queue rate dipped from 18k -> 9k in ~90s. 503s down from 12% -> 4%.
ryan: autoscaler still failing to request more nodes due to provider limit; but reduced load buys time.
maya: opening emergency ticket with provider support (PRIORITY: P1). reference: scale requests returned quotaExceeded id 0x9f3.
maya: provider: "we can approve burst request to 50% of asked capacity if you accept preemptible nodes." Options: accept preemptible mix (short-term) or wait for quota increase.
cal: short-term accept preemptible to handle surge. confirm with SRE?
ryan: agree. preemptible + fallback quantized models keeps customer latency near SLO vs full outages.
cal: executing acceptance. patching fleet config.
cal: ```
fleetctl update pool eu-west-1 --add-instance-type g4dn.xlarge:preemptible:50
```
cal: applied. provisioning started. autoscaler still logs `acknowledged scale request` -> provisioning stream.
ops-bot: provider-ticket: 987654 created, ETA 00:36 UTC for manual quota bump.
june: monitoring customer-facing errors; posting to CS channel to inform customers in affected regions. drafting status.
june: status msg to CS: "Experiencing degraded inference performance for a subset of requests in EU-WEST. Engineers are mitigating and routing heavy traffic to fallback region. Minimal data loss risk. Updates soon."
cal: can we capture a postmortem checklist now so we don't forget action items?
ryan: adding live notes: 1) update autoscaler to surface provider quota limit earlier 2) add a soft-threshold to trigger fallback before queue grows > 5k 3) reserve a small standby pool in eu-west for midnight window 4) improve runbook for provider quota escalations 5) telemetry: track scale_limit_reached metric.
maya: + action: add automated pre-approval flow with provider for short burst requests (so we don't wait 30-45m).
liam: + action: make model_fallback a canary toggle with automatic ramp down if latency is too high.
cal: current numbers: queue 6.2k, 503s 1.2%, avg latency 980ms (was 1.8s). preemptible nodes are coming up (3 -> 12 nodes live).
june: CS posted update and customer DMs for top 10 tenants with highest error rates.
cal: once preemptibles are stable, we'll start scaling down fallback and unpause batch jobs.
ryan: also note autoscaler misinterprets `scale_down suppressed` events; need clearer signals to avoid oscillation during mixed-instance provisioning.
cal: agreed. next steps: short-term: keep preemptible mix until provider approves quota increase. mid-term: runbook + autoscaler fix + reserved standby. owners: maya (provider pre-approval flow), ryan (autoscaler changes), liam (routing/fallback flag), june (CS comms & postmortem).
maya: documenting timeline for postmortem. will own timeline and publish within 48h.
cal: great. if no further regressions after 30m we'll close pager. monitoring for next 60m.
ops-bot: :white_check_mark: incident INC-2026-1345 status updated -> mitigation in progress, next update @ 00:30 UTC.
ryan: quick note for postmortem: include a replay of the autoscaler logs and the exact provider responses (429 vs 503) and throttling thresholds we hit.
cal: thanks team. passing to night squad for watch. handing off to maya as incident lead for postmortem and follow-ups. @maya you're the lead.
maya: taking lead. ping me for any follow-ups. :eyes:
liam: leaving a short ops note: `reduce default scale request chunk to 10 nodes` to avoid big all-or-nothing requests.
june: closing loop with CS: customers replied — most appreciated the proactive DM. no escalations to legal.
cal: handing off to oncall rotation. good job. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PAGE RESOLVED: queue stabilized, fallbacks active, provider approved temporary quota increase at 00:28 UTC. incident escalated to postmortem.
